questions.solution:
According to Doppler's effect, whenever there is relative motion between a source of sound and listener, the apparent frequency of sound heard by the listener is different from the actual frequency of sound emitted by the source. Let $S$ be source of sound and $L$ the listener of sound. Let $ν$ be the actual frequency of sound emitted by the source and $\lambda$ be the actual wavelength of the sound emitted.

If $v$ is velocity of sound in still air, then
$\lambda = \dfrac{v}{ν}$
If velocity of listener is ${v}_{L}$ and velocity of source is ${v}_{s}$, then apparent frequency of sound waves heard by the listener is
$ν ' = \dfrac{v - {v}_{L}}{v - {s}_{s}} \times ν$
Here, both source and listener are approaching each other.

Then ${v}_{s}$ is positive and ${v}_{L}$ is negative.
$∴ ν ' = \dfrac{v - \left(- {v}_{L}\right)}{v - {v}_{s}} \times ν = \left(\dfrac{v + {v}_{L}}{v - {v}_{s}}\right)ν$
$⇒ ν ' > ν$
Also, $\lambda ' < \lambda$
So, listener listens more frequency and observes less wavelength.
